recommendation: Keep this source fix as-is. It completes the previously partial FHIR-20607 application without changing the Request.intent immutability rule or reopening broader RequestStatus wording.
issue_request: FHIR-20607 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for R5 and asked to align Request immutability wording by removing inappropriate narrative uses of immutable while preserving Request.intent as the element expected to be immutable. Its resolution also directed clearer related basedOn/replaces wording: keep the terminal-state sentence for replaced targets and add the same-intent sentence after it.
initial_application: Jira records Git 193d552d63 as the application commit. That commit applied the main compound-request immutability wording, but it replaced the existing replaces terminal-state sentence with the new same-intent sentence instead of adding the same-intent sentence after it.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists request as an active logical pattern, so source/request/request-spreadsheet-notes.xml is current build input. Later FHIR-38868 changed the same narrative from requisitionId to groupIdentifier, and later RequestStatus cleanup replaced the historical cancelled status with current ended/completed/revoked terminology. The current Request.intent element comment still carries the intended immutable guidance, and Request.replaces is defined as completed or terminated request(s).
reconciliation: Added a single sentence to source/request/request-spreadsheet-notes.xml before the existing same-intent guidance, stating that in a replaces relationship the target resource is no longer in force and should have an ended status such as completed or revoked, or another terminal state supported by that resource.
source_changes: source/request/request-spreadsheet-notes.xml: restored the terminal-state part of the basedOn/replaces contrast using current ended/completed/revoked terminology.

related_jiras.note: Renamed the same compound-request narrative from requisitionId to groupIdentifier, explaining why current wording differs from the original FHIR-20607 resolution text.
Aligned request-status wording away from cancelled/suspended toward revoked/on-hold; this supports using current ended/completed/revoked terminology in the restored sentence.
